title: What If the Moon Were Twice as Close to Earth?

scenes.text: What if the Moon were twice as close? The oceans would notice first.
It would look twice as wide in the sky, and solar eclipses would happen more often.
Tides would be about eight times higher. Some islands would spend much of every day underwater.
Heavily populated coastlines could become uninhabitable, flooded by the sea twice a day.
A closer pull would flex Earth's crust, possibly setting off more earthquakes and eruptions, a bit like Io at Jupiter.
And it couldn't happen overnight. Only a massive object passing at just the right moment could do it, and the move would take many years.
